title: Constrained Learning with Non-Convex Losses
authors: Luiz F. O. Chamon, Santiago Paternain, Miguel Calvo-Fullana, Alejandro Ribeiro
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, vol. 69, no. 3, pp. 1739--1760
conclusions: Establishes a constrained counterpart of classical PAC learning theory ('near-PACC learnability') for constrained empirical risk minimization, including non-convex losses (Theorem 1, Corollary 1).

Shows the empirical dual problem (unconstrained, deterministic) has a bounded duality gap vs. the original non-convex constrained statistical problem, decomposed into a functional duality gap, a parametrization/approximation gap, and a sample/empirical gap.

Proves strong duality holds for the functional (infinite-dimensional) constrained learning problem even under non-convex losses, given mild non-atomicity/decomposability conditions (Proposition III.2).

Proposes a practical primal-dual (dual-ascent) algorithm (Algorithm 1): minimize the Lagrangian over parameters for fixed multipliers, then update multipliers via a projected ascent step on the constraint slacks, with near-optimality/near-feasibility guarantees (Theorems 2-3).

Demonstrates the framework on two applications: adversarially-robust image classification (CNN, non-convex) and rate-constrained fair classification on COMPAS (logistic model, non-convex 0/1-loss constraint via sigmoid surrogate), showing the dual multiplier rises to enforce a violated constraint and then stabilizes/shrinks once satisfied.
